note: A CENSUS REFRESH REDDENS MORE THAN census-check CAN SEE. The Underworld refreshed the canonical census (884.6 s on lefford at 223e7d57, 76 of 224 columns moved, schema unchanged). The census-check golden-pins tripwire flagged 14 mismatched literals across SIX calibration batteries. The full workspace suite found TEN reddened fixture-pin batteries. The four census-check misses read studies or derived surfaces that golden-pins.sql does not mount: branches_family_calibration homophony_count_is_measured_and_pinned, gathering_calibration pop_weighted_abs_latitude_reads_below_the_uniform_sphere_baseline, anomaly_injection the_falsified_recall_is_pinned_as_a_witness, and the spinning_eternal half of calibration a_frozen_sky_never_heads_a_cyclic_pantheon (its FIRST assert panics, so the second is never reached and its drift is invisible until you fix the first). SO: census-check is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT after a refresh. Re-pin six batteries, watch census-check go green, and you are still red. Run the workspace suite as well and take the new values from the assertion messages rather than transcribing them out of the census. TWO MORE FACTS FROM THE SAME RUN. Whole-workspace cargo nextest and cargo test now need HV_TEST_OK=1: a hook refuses them and points at make sluice-stage, which is right for gating and wrong when you only need to read failure messages. And the shared canonical worktree on lefford routinely holds an UNCOMMITTED docs/timings.md ledger row from a previous session, which census-run.sh discards with reset --hard. Check it before dispatching. Mine turned out to be a duplicate of a row already committed on main, but it would have been a silently lost 855.5 s measurement otherwise.
